html:
Niels Bohr was a Danish physicist whose model of the atom of 1913 was a founding step of quantum physics. He won the Nobel Prize in 1922.

In Bohr's model electrons move only in fixed orbits and give off light when they jump between them, which explained the colours of hydrogen. His institute in Copenhagen, opened in 1921, drew young physicists such as Heisenberg, and the Copenhagen interpretation of quantum mechanics is named after it. He argued with Einstein for decades about what the theory meant.

In 1943 he fled occupied Denmark to Sweden, as did most of the Danish Jews, and went on to the atomic bomb project in the United States. After the war he pressed for openness about nuclear weapons.
